candidates.title: Periphery megacity outperforms planned Western city on livability
candidates.shift: A first-person essay argues children/families find dense, less-planned Mexico City more livable than well-planned Vancouver, challenging the assumed superiority of North American planning norms.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative reframing: periphery urban form as a livability benchmark rather than a deficiency to fix — could inform how North American retail districts prioritize density/walkability over car-oriented planning.
candidates.evidence: Strong Towns essay comparing family experience in Mexico City vs Vancouver.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from Western planning norms as default aspiration to periphery megacities setting livability benchmarks; driven by lived density/walkability preference; could reshape North American mixed-use retail district design.

candidates.title: Cultural retail anchors a multi-ethnic periphery village
candidates.shift: A bookstore built in a historic, multi-ethnic Yunnan village positions retail-as-cultural-hub in a rural, non-metropolitan setting rather than a city center.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative single instance: rural/cultural retail formats gaining traction as tourism and community anchors outside major cities, a peripheral geography setting rather than following a retail standard.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily feature on Librairie Avant-Garde Huize Baiwu Bookstore by Jiakun Architects, Baiwu Village, Yunnan.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from urban-centric cultural retail to rural/periphery cultural-retail anchors; driven by heritage tourism narratives; could inform small-format retail-as-cultural-infrastructure in emerging markets.
candidates.author: 韩爽 - HAN Shuang

candidates.title: Transit infrastructure repurposed into cultural space in Central Asia
candidates.shift: A historic tram depot in Tashkent converted into a contemporary art centre exemplifies adaptive reuse of obsolete transit infrastructure in a non-Western capital.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: peripheral-geography adaptive reuse example that could set a template developers elsewhere follow for repurposing orphaned industrial/transit buildings into retail-adjacent cultural space.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen report on Studio KO's Centre for Contemporary Arts Tashkent inside a former tram depot.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from demolition to adaptive reuse of obsolete transit infrastructure; driven by cultural investment and heritage value; if it spreads, more commercial developers may target orphaned industrial buildings.
candidates.author: Lizzie Crook

candidates.title: Incremental, occupant-led urban renewal as expansion model
candidates.shift: A design studio's own office expansion into an adjacent bay in a Chinese urban renewal district models informal incremental renewal rather than top-down masterplanning.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: a single practice-level experiment suggesting tenant-driven incremental renewal could offer a lower-capital model for small retail/office tenants expanding in aging urban districts.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily report on Modum Atelier's office extension via incremental urban renewal in Guochuang Park.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from top-down masterplanned redevelopment to incremental, occupant-led renewal; driven by practice-level experimentation; could offer low-capital expansion model for small retail/office tenants.
candidates.author: 韩爽 - HAN Shuang

candidates.title: Road-land allocation as a growth constraint in periphery cities
candidates.shift: Cities dedicating far less land to roads (Dhaka, Kolkata, Nairobi at 10-14% vs Manhattan/London ~26%) are framed as structurally constraining mobility and commerce growth.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative reframing of a known stat as an absence — no target ratio/code exists for road-land allocation in fast-growing cities, which could reshape logistics-access standards for retailers expanding there.
candidates.evidence: Reddit post citing land-use percentage comparison across Manhattan, London, Dhaka, Kolkata, Nairobi.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from ad hoc road networks to a recognized target ratio in emerging megacities; driven by growth pressure in the Global South; could reshape retailer site-selection and logistics-access planning there.

candidates.title: Women's safety as codified design criterion for public space
candidates.shift: Urban design analysis names specific factors (lighting, sightlines, escape routes) as evaluative criteria for public/semi-public space, formalizing gendered-risk assessment.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative reframing: could push developers toward formal 'safety audit' standards for parking lots, plazas, and store entries as a design/insurance differentiator.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily feature analyzing four public spaces through a women's-safety lens.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from generic 'safe design' language to codified gendered-safety criteria; driven by advocacy and lived-experience research; could create new design/insurance standards for retail entries and parking.
candidates.author: Olivia Poston

candidates.title: Rising per-sqm costs squeeze small design galleries out of prime space
candidates.shift: Emerging design galleries report prohibitive exhibition-space quotes (e.g. £900/sqm), pushing them toward grassroots/alternative venues in London.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative early indicator: small-format independent retail/gallery economics may foreshadow broader square-footage cost pressure pricing out independents in major design capitals.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen feature citing a £900/sqm exhibition-space quote during London Design Festival lead-up.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from affordable pop-up exhibition space to prohibitively priced short-term retail/gallery space in prime design capitals; driven by real estate scarcity; independents get pushed to peripheral venues.
candidates.author: Jennifer Hahn
